name: China (mainland)
summary: Mainland China's two stock exchanges, in Shanghai and Shenzhen, both opened in December 1990. Together they form one of the world's largest stock markets by value. Local shares (A-shares) trade in renminbi under special rules: daily price limits, 100-share buy lots and no selling on the day of purchase. Foreign private investors usually reach them through Stock Connect in Hong Kong.

currency.name: Chinese yuan (renminbi)
currency.note: A-shares are priced in yuan, so a euro investor carries currency risk: moves of the yuan against the euro change the value of holdings in euros (Category L).

source.title: FTSE Equity Country Classification Process, v3.5, October 2026, Appendix 3 (FTSE Russell, PDF)

exchanges.name: Shanghai Stock Exchange (SSE)
exchanges.hours: Opening call auction 09:15–09:25, continuous trading 09:30–11:30 and 13:00–14:57, closing call auction 14:57–15:00. Lunch break 11:30–13:00.
exchanges.note: Home of the Main Board and, since 2019, the STAR Market for science and technology companies.

exchanges.name: Shenzhen Stock Exchange (SZSE)
exchanges.hours: Same as Shanghai: opening call auction 09:15–09:25, continuous trading 09:30–11:30 and 13:00–14:57, closing call auction 14:57–15:00.
exchanges.note: Runs the Main Board and the ChiNext market (launched October 2009) for growth companies.

indexes.name: CSI 300
indexes.description: The 300 largest and most liquid A-share stocks from Shanghai and Shenzhen. Base 1,000 points on 31 December 2004, published since 8 April 2005; reviewed twice a year. Calculated by China Securities Index Co.

indexes.name: SSE Composite Index
indexes.description: All eligible shares and depositary receipts listed in Shanghai. Base 100 points on 19 December 1990, the exchange's first trading day; published since 15 July 1991.

source.title: SSE Composite Index (China Securities Index Co.)

regulators.name: China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC)
regulators.role: Supervises the securities and futures markets, including both stock exchanges, which are self-regulated legal entities under its supervision.

investorProtection.name: Deposit insurance (People's Bank of China)
investorProtection.text: Bank deposits are protected up to RMB 500,000 per depositor and bank, under the Deposit Insurance Regulations in force since 1 May 2015.

investorProtection.name: Hong Kong Investor Compensation Fund (for Stock Connect)
investorProtection.text: Since 1 January 2020, the Hong Kong Investor Compensation Fund also covers Northbound trading through Stock Connect, for example if a Hong Kong broker defaults.

settlement.cycle: Shares settle on the trade day (T); cash on T or T+1
settlement.csd: China Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation (ChinaClear / CSDC)
settlement.note: Shares bought on one day can only be sold from the next trading day (no day trading), also for Stock Connect investors.

source.title: Stock Connect Information Book for Investors, version 6 July 2026, section 4.2 (HKEX, PDF)

rules.title: Daily price limits
rules.text: A-shares may only trade within a band around the previous close: ±10% on the Main Boards, ±20% on the STAR Market and ChiNext, and 5% for shares under risk warning. Orders outside the band are rejected.

rules.title: Buy in lots of 100, sell from the next day
rules.text: Buy orders must be in multiples of 100 shares (STAR Market: at least 200 shares). Shares bought on trade day T can only be sold from T+1.

source.title: Stock Connect Information Book for Investors, sections 3.11–3.12 (HKEX, PDF)

rules.title: Foreign ownership limits
rules.text: A single foreign investor may hold at most 10% of a listed company's shares, and all foreign investors together at most 30% of its A-shares, across all access channels.

rules.title: Stock Connect daily quota
rules.text: Northbound buying through Stock Connect is capped by a daily net-buy quota of RMB 52 billion each for Shanghai and Shenzhen. It resets every day.

source.title: Stock Connect Information Book for Investors, section 3.4 (HKEX, PDF)

taxes.glance: Via Stock Connect: 10% Chinese tax withheld on dividends (treaty refund possible); no Chinese capital gains tax; 0.05% stamp duty on the seller since 28 August 2023.

items.title: Dividends (Stock Connect)
items.text: Hong Kong and overseas investors pay 10% tax on cash dividends and bonus shares, withheld by the listed company. Investors from a treaty country with a lower rate can apply to the Chinese tax authority for a refund of the difference.

items.title: Capital gains (Stock Connect)
items.text: Hong Kong and overseas investors are exempt from capital gains tax and business tax on A-shares traded through Stock Connect (notice of the Ministry of Finance, State Taxation Administration and CSRC, 14 November 2014).

items.title: Stamp duty
items.text: 0.05% of the value of each A-share trade, paid by the seller only. It was halved from 0.1% on 28 August 2023.

items.title: For an Austrian investor
items.text: An Austrian bank can credit foreign withholding tax up to 15% of the dividend against Austrian KESt (Category Q), so the 10% Chinese tax can usually be credited in full.

sources.title: Stock Connect FAQ, section 5 (taxes), version 6 July 2026 (HKEX, PDF)
Stock Connect Information Book for Investors, section 7 (fees and taxes) (HKEX, PDF)

access: Stock Connect: brokers with access to the Hong Kong exchange can route orders for eligible Shanghai and Shenzhen shares (Northbound trading). Not every Austrian bank or broker offers this.
Many large Chinese companies also list H-shares in Hong Kong (in Hong Kong dollars), and some have depositary receipts in the US.
Indirectly, through funds or ETFs on Chinese, Asian or emerging-market indexes (Category H).
companies: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China

history.text: The Shanghai Stock Exchange is established on 26 November and starts operations on 19 December; the Shenzhen Stock Exchange is established on 1 December.
Shenzhen launches the ChiNext market for growth companies (October).
Shanghai Connect launches on 17 November, linking Hong Kong and Shanghai.
Shanghai's STAR Market debuts; the first 25 companies start trading on 22 July.
Stamp duty on A-share trades is halved to 0.05% from 28 August.

funFacts: The Shanghai Stock Exchange's first home was the Astor House Hotel on the old financial street near the Bund.
All of mainland China uses one time zone (UTC+8) and has no daylight saving time, so both exchanges keep the same hours all year.

sources.title: Stock Connect Information Book for Investors, version 6 July 2026 (HKEX, PDF)
